title: Rewards Ledger Standard: Points Reversal and the Zero Balance Floor (Pals Rewards and Tailwise Plus)
content:
**Scope.** Reversals of **Pals Rewards and Tailwise Plus** points after a refund, and what a reversal may do to the points balance and to certificates.

**Retired clause.** The clause under which, when a purchase that earned points was refunded in whole or in part and the tier takes points back on refund, the points it earned were taken back in proportion to the refunded share of its qualifying spend, rounded down, never more than the purchase earned, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the points reversed.

**Balance floor.** Where the tier does not allow a negative balance, a reversal larger than the current points balance takes the balance to 0 and the remainder is waived. No tier allows a negative balance.

**Certificates.** Certificates already issued are not cancelled by a reversal.

**Worked case (hypothetical figures).**

| Balance before | Points to be reversed | Balance after | Points waived |
|---|---|---|---|
| 900 | 300 | 600 | 0 |
| 120 | 300 | 0 | 180 |
| 300 | 300 | 0 | 0 |

**Questions the standard settles.**
- *The customer turned 1,000 points into a $5.00 certificate before the refund; does the reversal claw the certificate back?* No. Certificates already issued are not cancelled by a reversal; only the points balance moves, and never below 0.

superseded_clauses: When a purchase that earned points is refunded in whole or in part and points_reversal_on_refund is true, the points it earned are taken back in proportion to the refunded share of its qualifying spend, rounded down, never more than the purchase earned.
